title: Lord of the Rings – more government projects
content:
3 December 2001

Lord of the Rings – more government projects

  • Pete Hodgson
Foreign Affairs and Trade

Cabinet minister Pete Hodgson today announced further Government initiatives to maximise the benefits for New Zealand from the forthcoming release of The Lord of the Rings movies.

“These projects supplement those announced by the Prime Minister on November 7,” said Mr Hodgson, the minister appointed by Cabinet to oversee Lord of the Rings related projects. “We now have a broad range of initiatives to make sure we capture the maximum benefit for tourism, the New Zealand film industry and international understanding of this country’s exceptional creative talent and technology.”

The further projects are:
* A New Zealand screen industry production guide for international use, providing information on locations, infrastructure, film investment opportunities and New Zealand productions.

* Promotional videos highlighting New Zealand talent, innovation and creativity, particularly in the cultural, film and high-tech sectors.

* Expansion of the Film NZ website into a comprehensive portal for New Zealand film, film investment and tourism promotion.

* Development of LOTR-themed New Zealand stands at upcoming international film trade markets – Locations Expo and American Film Market in Los Angeles, Production Guide in London and the Cannes Film Festival.

* Technology and innovation workshops in Los Angeles, Silicon Valley and Seattle, showcasing New Zealand’s postproduction and digital effects capabilities.

* An inward investment mission, bringing key decisionmakers in the international screen production industry to New Zealand to promote film opportunities.

* An exhibition of New Zealand-produced LOTR models and props at a Los Angeles gallery, promoted to key figures in the US film production sector.

* A New Zealand reception at Oscar time for senior US and other filmmakers to promote New Zealand as a production location.

The total budget for these initiatives is $875,000. A small number of further projects are still under consideration.

“New Zealand will be well represented in events in 14 cities over the next few weeks to coincide with the opening of The Fellowship of the Ring,” Mr Hodgson said. “The projects I have announced today will follow up this initial burst of publicity with a sustained effort to promote New Zealand talent and innovation to the world.”

Industry New Zealand and the Ministry of Economic Development will carry out an economic impact assessment of the Government’s LOTR strategy by May 2002.

The Lord of the Rings
Further projects announced by Hon Pete Hodgson
3 December 2001
LOTR Production Guides

Lead Agencies - Investment NZ, Film NZ and NZ Film Commission

 A New Zealand screen industry production guide - including information on New Zealand locations, infrastructure, investment opportunities in film and a listing of New Zealand produced film - themed around LOTR and including interviews of all of the key players in the production of the Trilogy. $80,000
New Zealand Talent and Film Videos

Lead Agency - Creative NZ

 Promotion reels highlighting New Zealand talent, innovation and creativity, particularly in the cultural, film and hi-tech sector. $100,000
Internet Portal

Lead Agencies - Film NZ, Investment NZ

 To use the Film NZ web portal as an effective web portal that will effectively act as a portal for film, film investment and tourism promotion. This will include hot links to all key players in these sectors (including Investment NZ, Trade NZ, MFAT, Tourism NZ, Industry NZ, NZ Film Commission). It will include a fact sheet on LOTR, the LOTR locations and possibly images from the movies. $60,000
Film Trade Markets

Lead Agencies - Investment NZ, Film NZ, MFAT, NZ Film Commission

 Locations Expo, Los Angeles
American Film Market, Los Angeles
Cannes Film Festival, Cannes
Production Guide, London

Creation of New Zealand stands with LOTR theme, creation of LOTR flyers and use of footage from LOTR at the events. Targeted receptions and dinners with the specific objective of increasing sales of New Zealand film and increased production of films into New Zealand.

 $180,000
Technology and Innovation Workshops

Lead Agency - Investment NZ

 The first of 3 in a series of workshops in Los Angeles, Silicon Valley and Seattle focused on the special effects in LOTR engineered by New Zealand's Weta Ltd and providing opportunities to promote links to Weta and other NZ hi-tech companies. Target audience: major Hollywood studios, special effects companies, location managers, producers, venture capital firms, corporate and financial investor contacts. $200,000
Inward Mission
Lead Agency - Investment NZ		 An inward mission targeting decision makers of up to six people in the screen production industry. $130,000
LA Exhibition
Lead Agency - MFAT		 Professionally mounted exhibition of film models and props from the likes of Weta Workshop created for LOTR. These would be shown at a Los Angeles gallery with targeted invitations to key players in the US film sector. $45,000
Oscar Events
Lead Agency - MFAT		 A reception at a prestigious Los Angeles location featuring New Zealand food, wine and displays for up to 100 senior Hollywood and foreign filmmakers to celebrate LOTR and to promote New Zealand as a film location. $80,000
subject to nominations
Total   $875,000
